_comment: Shared by the Godot game (game/) and the Python backend (backend/). Units: robot mm, world cm.

robot._z_note: Z is reported by the backend in abstract 'z units' (0..z_max) derived from the STS3020 ID1 drum servo count (SERVO_STATUS abs=). The firmware has no Z homing; the backend defines 0 at the position seen when 'z_set top' is sent. If a LARGER value means the arm is HIGHER set z_up_is_positive=true. The on-screen rope is longest when the arm is highest (inverse mapping).

world._fit_note: true: the robot's X range spans the play area width (computed at runtime from the window, the debug panel and the projection); false: fixed travel_x_cm.

render._fullscreen_note: The screen is portrait, 9:16 (#157): design size 720 x 1280, the exhibit's monitor is 1080 x 1920 (or 2160 x 3840) standing on end. The monitor is turned in the OS's display settings, never inside the game. fullscreen: true = the game fills the monitor (also --fullscreen / --windowed on the command line, F11 while it runs). On a monitor of another shape the picture keeps its 9:16 and gets bars at the sides: nothing is cut off or stretched. docs/display_setup.md.

audio._note: Sound effects from 効果音ラボ (soundeffect-lab.info). In game/assets/audio/ as part of the game; do not hand the files out on their own (see SOURCES.md there). up/down = the UFO rising/sinking on screen (arm going down/up).

pose_direction._note: Hand shape per direction (robot axes [x, y, z]; +X right, +Y away, +Z arm up). open = パー, peace = チョキ, fist = グー, point = 指差し (only the index out), thumb_up / thumb_down = いいね (index..pinky folded, thumb out) with the thumb towards the top / bottom of the camera view as shown (view flip_v and joystick invert_z apply; within thumb_min_vertical of vertical, else no sign). Default: point = where the finger points, thumbs-up up / down = arm up / down, claw: open (パー) = open, peace (チョキ) = closed, held claw_hold_ms; fist (グー) = nothing (rest the hand). "finger" = where the index finger points (any angle, or snapped to point_snap_deg; image -> robot axes with the joystick invert_x / invert_y / swap_xy; shorter than point_min_len hand sizes = pointing at the camera = no motion). A shape counts after pose_confirm_ms; a confirmed one survives a flicker shorter than pose_release_ms; another shape stops first, then arms again. After a forced stop the shape must be gone for pose_release_ms. A shape used for a direction never moves the claw. Untested with the real camera / robot.

gesture._note: Pinch hand joystick (backend: --gesture). enabled = only the default of a game started without start.sh (Godot directly): start.sh always passes --gesture or --no-gesture (gestures are on with ./start.sh and ./start.sh --mock, off with --game-only / --no-gesture). scheme = how the game reads the hand (pinch_joystick = this pinch stick, pose_direction = a hand shape per direction; settings of other schemes go in schemes.<id>; switching always stops the gesture). delegate = gpu (Metal: faster, and frees the CPU for the game). MediaPipe 1.1.1's GPU path keeps one image per frame (~1 GB per 30 s, aborting after ~8 min with 'Error creating pixel buffer: -6662') until the landmarker is closed, so it is rebuilt on a thread and swapped in every gpu_recreate_s. detection_confidence / tracking_confidence = MediaPipe's thresholds (tracking low so a fast, blurred hand is kept). pinch_start 1.0 / pinch_release 1.5 / confirm 0 were tuned by hand on the C270 (open the hand wide to release: check the ratio goes above 1.5). stale_ms = an event older than this stops the stick (CPU MediaPipe frames occasionally take 200-280 ms on an M4 MacBook Air; 150 stopped every few seconds). camera = part of the gesture camera's name (or an index). Pinch = |thumb tip - index tip| / hand size (the larger of |index MCP - pinky MCP| and 0.75 x |wrist - middle MCP|): starts <= pinch_start held pinch_confirm_ms, ends >= pinch_release held release_confirm_ms (tunable live from the debug panel: the gesture_config command). A hand lost (or a second hand / ambiguous) for less than lost_grace_ms keeps the last good frame (MediaPipe drops a moving hand for a frame or two). min_confidence gates the left/right score (0 = off: it drops for a hand seen from above). roi = operating region [x0, y0, x1, y1] in normalised image coords (keep it outside the crane's reach). joystick: radius = fraction of the image short side, deadzone / full = fractions of the radius, speed = ((r - deadzone)/(full - deadzone))^curve * max_speed_mm_s. allow_real_robot: true since the gesture was checked with the mock (2026-10-25); the robot must still be connected, motors on, homed, no alarm, nothing else moving (H toggles the mode).

stabilize._note: #118: the arm hangs on ball chains and swings. The backend opens the focus camera (match) with OpenCV while the game watches, measures each frame's motion with optical flow (Lucas-Kanade corners, translation + rotation), cancels the part faster than cutoff_hz (a deliberate XY move is followed with a short lag), zooms by zoom to hide the moved edges, and streams JPEG on its own port (never on the robot's connection). The game shows it as the focus camera (scope, panels, the study mode's photo) and opens the camera itself only when the stream stops. max_shift = the largest correction (fraction of the width). Display only.

scope._note: The arm camera as a round aiming scope in the right column of the score game (#141): camera.focus, or camera.overview when the arm has no camera; hidden with no camera at all. It shows the hub's picture, so the stabilized one whenever the backend streams it (camera.focus.stabilize, #118: the shake is cancelled with optical flow in the backend; not with --game-only, which has no backend). zoom 1..4 crops the middle. Display only.

camera._note: USB cameras by role (C270 = overview / gesture, Innomaker U20CAM = arm tip): overview = looks down on the desk (gesture detection later), focus = on the arm tip. match = part of the camera name (empty = none; pick one in the debug panel). The scope view shows focus, or overview when there is no focus camera. Frames are only drawn: never saved or sent.

settings_screen._note: The settings screen (#93, the gear on the title screen): what it may change (#96: this section was config/settings_schema.json). It saves only these keys, only changed from game_config.json, to config/local_settings.json (not in Git); the game and the backend read that file over game_config.json and ignore any key or value not allowed here (a hand-edited file cannot change the calibration or the safety settings). Types: bool, enum (options: [value, label]), number (min, max, step), text (max_length). apply = when a saved change is used: now (the game applies it on 保存), restart (the next start of the game), backend (the next start of the backend: ./start.sh again).

title_screen._calibration_first_note: #114: when the title shows at start, the settings screen's 校正 tab opens over it first (its 0. AI・外部サービス checks Jev / the tutor AI / Claude Code / VOICEVOX as soon as the backend is up); closing it (Esc) shows the title.
title_screen._note: The first screen (#90): pick the study mode or the game mode; Esc comes back. Skipped when headless (tests / CI), with --no-title, and when the start is already decided (--study-mode / --study-demo / --scenario / --capture / --log-motion / --gesture-demo, or study_mode.autostart); --title shows it anyway. Presentation only: while it shows, the arm takes no manual input, gestures included (Space still stops); the debug panel opens above it (F1 / Tab).

study.system_prompt: あなたは画像を見ながら学習を支援する家庭教師です。答えだけでなく、考え方を段階的に日本語で説明してください。画像にない事実は推測と明記してください。
study._ai_note: #232: the study mode's AI. local (default) = the local LLM server at tutor_url only: the watch (each problem written or not) and the problem's place from POST /v1/sheet, the explanation from the tutor; Jev, Claude and Codex are never called by the study mode and no Jev key is needed. cloud = Jev + Claude / Codex as before (explain_provider still picks the explanation).
study._tutor_note: The study mode's explanation by the learning support AI (UFOくん API, #104): explain_provider tutor ("" = provider). Only the explanation goes there (one 10cm close-up and "N ばんが わからない"); the advice, the problem's place and the Study tab stay with provider. tutor_url = https://<the tutor PC>:8444 (http only on the same PC). The token (tutor_token_file; optional since #128: no file = no Authorization header, for a server started without one) and the server's self-signed cert (tutor_cafile, trusted alone, no host name check) are in config/secrets/, never in Git. Two failures in a row (tutor_fail_limit) rest it for tutor_cooldown_s; meanwhile and on any error the worksheet's own hints are used. When the problem is not in the picture it answers navigate: with the arm camera's calibration (calibration.json focus_camera, tools/calibrate_focus.py) the game looks again up to 60 mm away, at most twice (homework_navigate, then the usual staged capture). Check the link: python3 tools/check_tutor_api.py. Not yet run on the real robot.
study._note: The Study tab (camera study assistant). Optional and off by default. It runs only when enabled here and the backend is started with --study (./start.sh --study): two switches on purpose, as it sends camera frames to the assistant; start.sh stops with the reason when only --study is given. provider: claude (Claude Code CLI, signed in; claude is looked for in ~/.local/bin, Homebrew and the newest VS Code / Cursor extension when not on PATH; ~ is allowed) or codex (codex app-server). No tools, no MCP, no settings; no credentials are stored here.

approach._note: 近づいてアドバイス (#76): Z to the top, XY to the spot recorded with homework_spot_set (config/calibration.json homework_spot) or to a clicked overview point (#78), claws open (open_claw: the arm hangs from the rope and its camera cable can tilt it; standing on its open claws the camera looks straight down, so record the spot where the open claws stand on the worksheet), Z down to its height, wait for the game's capture (at most hold_timeout_s), Z back to the top (claws closed if close_claw_after), XY back to where it started (return_xy). Holds the motion lock like the auto catch; stop / soft_stop / motors off / the operator leaving / any fault end it with the robot's stop (ABORT). Not yet run on the real robot.

camera_map._note: Overview camera image -> CoreXY XY (#78): a homography fitted to points recorded in the 宿題 tab (arm camera centred on a mark, the mark clicked in the overview image), saved in config/calibration.json camera_xy. Not used to move when the fit's largest error is over max_error_mm, when the camera's size / flips changed since calibration, or for a point more than margin_mm outside the calibrated points. Not yet run on the real robot.

locate._note: Which problem to look at (#79): the study assistant (study.provider) names the problem the child is stuck on ("stuck": compares the frame at the last progress gain with the frame now) or the next one to solve ("next") and gives its answer box in pixels; Jev is asked for the same answer box and the arm moves only when the centre of the assistant's box lies inside Jev's box widened by jev_margin (0..1 of the image; require_jev false moves on the assistant's box alone). Moving needs a usable camera_map. Not yet run on the real robot.

docker._note: #112: ./start.sh starts the VOICEVOX ENGINE as its own Docker container (when it starts the backend and speech uses voicevox at 127.0.0.1 / localhost) and stops it when start.sh ends; Docker stopped -> colima is started (and stopped at the end). Bound to 127.0.0.1 only. The image is pinned (version and digest: cpu-0.26.0, 2026-10-23, arm64 / amd64). Prepared in the background: until it answers, the voice is say. A container of that name already running is used and left running.

cache._note: #171: a line made once (VOICEVOX / say) is kept as a file in this directory (relative to the repository root; not in Git) and the same line is played from it without asking the engine again; the files stay when the backend stops. Another speaker / sampling rate / say voice is another file. max_files: the least recently used go first. Delete the directory to make every line again.

speech._note: Voice for the helper (#79), tried in this order: a local VOICEVOX engine (voicevox_speaker = a style id from GET /speakers; the game shows the credit "VOICEVOX:<character>" the VOICEVOX terms ask for; check the character's own terms), then the macOS say command (say_voice). The WAV is made by the backend and played by the game.

helper._note: The game's helper (#79): when the backend reports a stall, say offer_text once (again after offer_repeat_s while still stalled). keys.stuck (or a thumbs-up held thumb_hold_ms within offer_window_s of the offer, only while the gesture control is off so the thumb never also moves the arm) locates the problem the child is stuck on and takes the arm's camera there; keys.next does it for the next problem to solve (H is the gesture on/off key). Thumbs-ups need the backend's hand camera (--gesture-camera).

homework._note: Homework watch (F1 panel tab). enabled = this watch in the F1 panel; the backend's homework service also starts when study_mode.enabled is true (the study mode uses it), and nothing is captured until a watch is started. While started, the overview camera is captured every interval_s and the worksheet's progress is estimated with Cloudflare Workers AI typesafe/jev-1.14.0 (method verified in ~/python_ws/jev: 3 questions per call, about 8.8k tokens / $0.00037 per call). The key is CF_ACCOUNT_ID / CF_API_TOKEN from the environment or the repository's .env (never committed; see .env.example). Frames go to Cloudflare and are not stored here. Stall: the shown progress has not grown by stall_min_gain points for stall_s (not at 100%, not while a hand covers the sheet); the panel then offers an advice by the study assistant (study.provider: Claude Code / Codex, no --study needed), and again only after another stall_s.

speed._safety: SPEED UP: the hand's stick and the arrow keys go up to boost_mm_s in XY while it lasts (Z never changes; the easy mode's automatic carry is not touched). Without it the hand is at gesture.joystick.max_speed_mm_s (60) and the keys at their usual speed. On the real crane the backend decides: its jog cap is backend.jog_max_mm_s (60) and becomes backend.jog_boost_mm_s (100) only while the jog_boost the game sends lasts; the backend ends it by itself, and at an emergency stop (the game ends it when the round stops). The 5 mm jog edge margin, the dead-man and the firmware's soft limits are unchanged. 100 mm/s is NOT verified on the real crane.

powerups._note: #188. enabled: the items appear at all. notice: the big name on the screen with its burst and shake (the small timers stay). sounds: the pickup's sound, and the music duck_db lower for duck_s under it. lights: the Dial's front LED (MULTI BALL) and the gold exhibition light (DOUBLE SCORE). debug_keys: while playing, F2 = SPEED UP, F3 = MULTI BALL (needs a ball on the field), F4 = DOUBLE SCORE now. An item appears first_spawn_s after GO, then every spawn_interval_s after the last one was taken or went away, with the chance spawn_chance (0..1); which one by weights (0 = never), at one of three spots, one at a time, for item_life_s. Speed and x2 run on timers (taking it again starts the time again, never stacks); MULTI BALL splits one ball into three but keeps one physical Dial cycle. Effects/lighting never hold robot motion or physics.

bgm._levels_note: #181: top = the title screen at start (the mode selection), menu = the score game's own title, tutorial = the practice, game = the 150 s clock, ending = the result; jingle = played once (not a loop, on the effects' bus) when a mode is chosen on the title screen, and the next music starts after it. No music in the settings screen's 校正 tab. No fades: a track starts and stops at once (it still steps back while a voice speaks). gain_db makes the tracks equally loud: measured with ffmpeg -i FILE -af ebur128 -f null - (integrated loudness, LUFS: top -21.0, intro -8.9, tutorial -4.9, game -18.0, ending -4.9) and brought to -18 LUFS; the jingle (-27.1) to -18. Other files: measure them and set gain_db = -18 - LUFS.
bgm._note: #173: the music from files in game/assets/audio/bgm/ (each machine puts its own there; the folder is not in Git, #151). menu = while a title screen shows (the mode selection at start, the score game's own title), game = while the 150 s clock runs, ending = the result and the ranking after a round. .mp3 / .ogg / .wav, played as a loop. A file that is not there: the round keeps the synthesised tune, the menu and the result stay silent. gain_db: each track's own level on top of audio.bgm_volume_db. files: false = never the files.

sounds._note: The score game's sounds (#143). files: true = the sound files of game/assets/audio/manifest.json (Kenney, CC0; where each came from is in that file and docs/audio_sources.md), false = only the sounds synthesised in the game (also what a missing file falls back to). pan 0..1: how far a Dial's sounds (absorb, drop, return, release, fault) are to the Dial's side (the left; #200: the only Dial). Volumes: audio.volume_db (effects), audio.sfx_volume_db / audio.bgm_volume_db (the buses), audio.sfx_enabled / audio.bgm_enabled.

scope._note: The arm camera as a round aiming scope in the right column of the score game (#141): camera.focus, or camera.overview when the arm has no camera; hidden with no camera at all. zoom 1..4 crops the middle.

result_bonus._note: The round's end bonuses (#153; docs/game_mode_spec.md §3.2), added to the score on the result screen: capsule_each x the capsules a Dial took before the time ran out (a late one and the practice capsule do not count), combo_each x the longest chain, jackpot_each x the jackpots won. final score = the score while playing + these. They are end bonuses only: the switch bonus (score.table.switch_bonus) and the jackpot's own points (score.table.jackpot) are paid while playing and are not added again. 0 = that bonus is left out. Tuning values, not final.

result_show._note: The result's show (#153), one timeline (seconds): YOUR SCORE comes up (intro_s), the number counts up (count_s) and stops (hold_s); then for each bonus: BONUS! and its points (announce_s), they fly into the number (absorb_s), the number runs on (bonus_count_s), a breath (bonus_hold_s); then the number shrinks (wind_up_s) and FINAL SCORE! hits and celebrates (final_s). tick_s: one counting blip per this long. strong_at: a bonus of this many points or more gets the strongest effects (less = weaker, never below 30 %). Every sound, shake, flash and spark of a moment starts in the same tick of this timeline. Enter skips to the end. With game_mode.effects false the final score is shown at once; render.screen_shake off keeps the picture still. Presentation only: no device is told anything.

ranking._note: The high scores (#155; docs/game_mode_spec.md §3.3): the ten best final scores (the score with its end bonuses) in user://game_mode/rankings.tsv (tab separated: rank, score, timestamp, id). No name is asked for or kept. A round that reached its result is offered by itself when the result's show is over; 0 points, a score that would be 11th or lower, the practice, a stopped round, the demo (--game-mode-demo) and a shortened round (--game-mode-seconds) make no record. enabled: false = no record and no board (the result ends as before). hold_s: how long the final score stands before NEW RECORD! / the board. record_s: how long NEW RECORD! is shown. Enter moves on at once.

real._xy_feed_note: #194: the feed (mm/min) of the easy mode's XY moves to a Dial: the carry, and the practice's easy_goto. 9000 = 150 mm/s. At backend.xy_fast_feed_mm_min (15900 = 265 mm/s, the firmware's top) a 45-degree move, where one motor does nearly all the steps (about 1.4 times an axis move's step rate), ended in the firmware's alarm 'timed segment queue lost position confidence' on the machine (2026-11-19), and the practice's moves were too quick to watch. At 9000 the one-motor step rate of a diagonal stays under that of an axis move at 15900, which ran. Leave this out to use backend.xy_fast_feed_mm_min again.

easy._note: The easy mode (#169; docs/game_mode_spec.md §3.4). #198: nobody chooses a difficulty any more (no config key, no D key, no fingers on the title): the easy mode is always what is played; where it cannot be used (no backend, another hand scheme) the manual hand control is played and the title says why. cancel_hold_s: while the backend waits for the destination, an open hand held this long gives the catch up (the claw opens, try again), longer than the short open hand that separates the fist from the fingers. The easy mode: (pinch = XY only; a fist held hold_s = catch here by itself; then one finger = carry to the portal, Dial 1 on the left; #200: there is no Dial 2 on the right any more and two fingers mean nothing). The practice shows the same. The easy mode needs the backend (its sequence runs there and holds the motion lock) and the pinch joystick scheme. wait_destination_s: how long the backend waits for the destination with the claw closed; after that it ends EXPIRED: nothing is moved or released, a person puts it right. request_timeout_s: the game waits this long for the backend's answer to easy_grab / easy_deliver before it stops in FAULT (never sent again by itself). dry_run: made-up drop points (XY mm) and release height (Z units) of the virtual crane only (--mock). The real crane's (Dial 1's XY, the catch height, the release height) are measured on the machine in the settings screen's 校正 tab, saved in config/calibration.json#easy_dials (not in Git), used only once confirmed there, and kept for the next sessions (recorded again only when Z is measured again). real: what is not a fact of the machine for the real crane's easy catch: tolerances, the claw settle time, the claw span bounds, how near home a limit switch is normal, the timeouts per step (s; a step that takes longer is a FAULT) and in total per part. The travel height is the Z top record, the XY feed backend.xy_feed_mm_min (xy_feed_mm_min here overrides it). auto_catch.real is not used by the easy mode.

tutorial._note: The practice before the score game (#149): Enter on the score game's title goes through it once per visit (the spell, the hand shapes one by one, one real capsule through a Dial), then the round starts from a full reset. enabled: false = Enter starts the round at once (T still starts the practice). mode: only read when game_mode.difficulty is missing (an older config); the practice shows the round's difficulty (#169). The hand steps' gauges fill in about 3 s (hold_s of open / pinch / z_pinch, move_s of move / z_move: override them in steps). The hard mode with the pinch joystick also teaches letting go (release: the shape that opens the claw) and the up / down mode (z_pinch: a pinch with the back of the hand to the camera; z_move: carried up or down). voice_link_wait_s: the first lines wait this long for the voice's link to come up (else the spell would be shown without its voice). debug_panel (game_mode.debug_panel): true keeps the debug panel open beside the score game (false: closed when it opens; F1 / Tab opens it). steps: {id: {title, sub, say, hold_s...}} overrides a step, modes: {mode: {hand scheme: [step ids]}} the order (game/scripts/tutorial/gesture_tutorial_steps.gd). Staff keys in the practice: F6 = the step again, F7 = the next step, F8 = leave the practice out.

timing._release_retries_note: #185: after RELEASE_DONE the Dial's switch is still on for the whole check (verify_retry_s x verify_tries = 2 s): the capsule did not leave, so RELEASE_BALL is sent once more, at most release_retries times, then FAULT. Needs the Dial firmware 0.4 (UFO-DeviceHub); an older Dial refuses the second release = FAULT as before. 0 = never again.

field._portrait_note: The field is tall since #157 (660 x 714, the screen is portrait): the capsule is seen falling all the way down. gravity_scale went 0.7 -> 0.85 with it so a capsule does not stay much longer than on the old wide field (measured over 60 capsules: 6.2 s on average, 11.9 s at most; the wide field: 4.9 s, 9.9 s). Where everything stands is in game/scripts/game_mode/pinball_field.gd and docs/game_mode_spec.md §4.

game_mode._note: SUMMON THE UFO, the 150 s score game (#138; the rules are docs/game_mode_spec.md). The title's third card (enabled). devices: auto (the backend's hub when the game uses the backend, else the Dials simulated inside the game) / mock / backend; with the backend, devicehub.enabled must be on (port mock = the backend's simulated hub). dials: left = Dial 1 (0x20 = 32), the only portal since #200 (a right entry is not read: nothing is sent to Dial 2, 0x21), color = its RGB on the screen and, sent as SET_DIAL_COLOR, the Dial's unit colour for its LEDs (the default is UFO-DeviceHub's own: cyan). dial_leds: the Dials' transfer LEDs follow the game (SET_DIAL_EFFECT, UFO-DeviceHub docs/game-mode-interface.md; firmware 0.3, older firmware answers UNSUPPORTED and the game goes on without). Every number here is a tuning value, not final: the score table and the timings (absorb_s + drop_s = the 1.1 s from the Dial's switch to the drop) are to be set by play tests and by measuring the real Dials. lights: the Illumination follows the game (best effort like dial_leds: a refusal never holds the game). visual_quality: high / low (low = a still, plain background for a slow machine; the game is the same). effects: false = no bounce, no light trails, no breathing glow (for debugging; the game is the same). trace: one JSON line per event in user://game_mode/trace_<time>.jsonl. Not yet run with the real Dials.

devicehub._note: The peripherals' hub (UFO-DeviceHub: ESP-NOW hub M5AtomS3R, Illumination ATOM, M5Dial x2), #108. The backend opens it (enabled) and the settings screen's テスト tab tests the devices through it, like UFO-DeviceHub's pc.web_console (which cannot run at the same time: one program per serial port). port: auto (every USB serial port in turn except the robot's (Core2) ports: the hub's auto-detect sends HELLO lines), a port name, or mock (a simulated hub, no hardware). system_id: which UFO system's hub (1 / 2; another system's hub is refused). The protocol and gateway are copies of UFO-DeviceHub's pc/ (backend/src/corexy_ufo_backend/devicehub/__init__.py says which commit). trace: a file for UFO-DeviceHub's own trace (every command, ACK and event of the hub as JSON Lines; "" = none; also the backend's --devicehub-trace), to join with the score game's trace (#138). Not yet run with the real hub from the game.

backend._claw_grip_note: #192: a claw closing to its recorded closed angle (閉じる / grab / the sequences' CLOSE_CLAW) grips the capsule a little before that angle; the firmware then answers SERVO_TURN ... result=TIMEOUT ... torque=ON. When it stopped within this many degrees of the target with the torque still on, the backend takes it as a grip (not a failure). Seen on the machine: 0.6 and 0.9 deg short (7 and 10 counts). 0 = every TIMEOUT is a failure, as before; at most 15. A tuning value: a thicker object stops farther away.
backend._xy_fast_feed_note: #179: the feed (mm/min) of the automatic XY moves that are to be as quick as the machine goes: to the middle of the stage after homing, and the easy mode's carry to a Dial (game_mode.easy.real.xy_feed_mm_min overrides it there). 15900 = just under the firmware's MAX_FEED_MM_MIN (15909.9 mm/min = 265 mm/s, 1000 mm/s2; a larger feed is clamped there). null = xy_feed_mm_min. NOT yet run at this feed on the real machine (lost steps, a carried capsule swinging): lower it here if it is too much.
backend._jog_boost_note: #188 (SPEED UP): while the game's boost lasts (the jog_boost command, sent by the game when the item is taken) a jog's XY cap is jog_boost_mm_s instead of jog_max_mm_s. The backend keeps the deadline (at most jog_boost_max_s per request) and goes back by itself; the emergency stop, motors off, jog_boost 0 or the last client leaving ends it at once (a soft_stop only stops the motion). The edge margin (jog_edge_margin_mm, jog_edge_slow_s), the dead-man and the firmware's soft limits are unchanged. Omit it or set it <= jog_max_mm_s for no boost. 100 mm/s is NOT verified on the real crane (the firmware's own jog cap is far above it): try it there before the exhibit.
backend._jog_edge_note: #185: a jog (the arrow keys, the hand stick) stays jog_edge_margin_mm inside the XY soft limits and slows down towards that line (speed towards an edge <= distance left / jog_edge_slow_s). Seen on the machine 2026-11-17: at 60 mm/s the hand stick ran to Y = 0.3 mm (the firmware's soft limit is at 0.5 mm), the home limit switch was pressed and the next jog ended in ALARM. 0 = off. Programmed moves (move_xy, the easy mode) are not changed.
backend._home_center_note: #175: after XY homing (the home command, and the 校正 tab's preparation) the arm goes on to the middle of the stage: the centre of robot.x_min..x_max / y_min..y_max, or home_center_mm [x, y] (mm; a point outside the soft limits is not used). An ordinary XY move at backend.xy_fast_feed_mm_min (#179), at the height homing already requires (the arm wound up). home_then_center false = it stays in the home corner as before.
backend._note: serial_rx_stall_s / serial_reopen_s (#161): a command sent and nothing at all read for serial_rx_stall_s = the link is dead although the port looks open (a USB hub's transaction error can stop the reading side alone: jogs still move, every command times out); the backend sends JOG 0 / ABORT blind (best effort, unconfirmed), drops the link (motors disabled, Z points forgotten) and, like after an unplugged cable, reopens the port every serial_reopen_s (0 = never). serial_port / serial_port_2: the Core2 boards used here (#100; set them in the settings screen, saved to local_settings.json): the one connected is opened (both: serial_port), none set = the first USB serial port found, ./start.sh --port wins. z_counts_per_unit: servo counts per abstract Z unit (4096 counts/turn; 3 turns = 12288 counts = 100 units). z_sign: +1 if positive SERVO_TURN raises the arm, -1 otherwise (set on the real machine). jog_max_mm_s: speed cap for serial JOG (firmware recommends <= 50 mm/s).

study_mode._note: UFOくん 勉強モード (#86). The title screen, F5, ./start.sh --study-mode or the game's --study-mode start it. enabled = the study mode is there, and the backend starts the homework service it needs (voice, per-problem watch, explanation) even when homework.enabled is false (homework.enabled is only the F1 panel's homework watch). Nothing is sent outside while demo.source is simulated. weekday_label = the day shown and said (fixed to Monday for the demo). grade = the first grade shown (nursery_1..3, elem_1..6, jhs_1..3; , / . change it on the intro screen). Worksheets: config/worksheets.json (python3 tools/build_worksheets.py; printable sheets in docs/worksheets/).

demo._note: What the study mode uses (#92). simulated = no camera, Jev or AI, nothing leaves the machine: the worksheet, the answers (keys 1/2/3), the problem's place (worksheet data + mock_desk) and the explanation (the worksheet's own hints) are simulated; the arm moves on a mock robot only (never the real crane). camera = the overview camera, Jev (Cloudflare) and Claude / Codex: frames are sent to them. Which robot is not set here: it is the one start.sh connected (./start.sh = the real crane, --mock = the backend's mock, --game-only = the game's own mock). With the real crane the backend still refuses what is not calibrated and confirmed below (the tidy-up separately). The earlier mode key is still read (mock = simulated, camera / real = camera).

mock_desk._note: mock robot only: where the A4 page lies in robot XY (page x -> robot +x, page y -> robot +y from origin, scaled by mm_per_paper_mm so the 297 mm page fits the 200 mm Y travel), to aim the mock arm at problem 3.

watch._note: Per-problem state from Jev's per-answer-box probability: >= filled_prob counts as a filled reading, >= writing_prob as writing, below as empty; a reading held (hand over the sheet, sheet not visible) changes nothing. A problem is filled after confirm_readings filled readings in a row (a later empty reading takes it back). The homework is complete after all 3 stayed filled for complete_readings readings in a row, or when a grown-up confirms it (Enter). Filled means written, never correct.

help._note: HELP looks at problem 3 (the challenge). key: the same key as the homework helper's stuck key (homework.helper.keys.stuck) by default. open_claw: open the claws before going down (false: the landing stays above the sheet with the claws closed).

hand_help._note: #136: while studying, a hand held to the overview camera with 1 / 2 / 3 fingers (point = index, peace = index + middle, three = index + middle + ring) for hold_ms makes UFOくん ask "問題 N、教えてあげようか？"; a thumbs-up held for hold_ms within offer_s starts the HELP for that problem (as Y does for help.problem: the overview camera finds it, the arm camera photographs it and the AI explains it; a problem already filled is explained too when asked by hand). The arm camera shows in the round view from the arm's first move, and its photo stays there while the explanation is spoken. Needs the hand tracking (./start.sh: on with the real robot / --mock). The hand never jogs the arm or moves the claw in the study mode. Not yet run on the real robot.

height._heights_note: #110: one close-up, the claw tips 10 cm above the desk (capture_heights_cm [10.0], no landing stage). The 校正 tab measures it from the Z calibration alone (calibration.json#study_height: the drum radius gives cm per Z, the Z bottom is the desk, camera_offset 0); [10.0, 5.0] and landing true bring the 5 cm and closest stages back.
height._note: Backend Z is an abstract unit, not a height above the desk. Z(camera h cm) = z_desk_tip + (z_up_is_positive ? +1 : -1) * (h - camera_offset_cm) * z_per_cm. z_desk_tip = Z where the claw tips touch the desk, z_per_cm = Z units per cm (measure with a block of known height), camera_offset_cm = lens above the claw tips, landing_tip_cm = claw tip height at the landing (below min_clearance_cm only with allow_landing_contact, after checking it on the robot). real: every null measured on the machine and every confirmed item set by hand, otherwise the staged descent is refused (NOT measured yet). dry_run: made-up values for the mock robot only.

cleanup._enabled_note: #110: false = no tidy-up at all: after the celebration the game unlocks at once (true = the magnet-jig tidy-up below, still refused on the real robot until enabled_real and measured).
cleanup._note: Tidy-up with a magnet jig: claws open over the jig's stand (jig_xy), down to jig_grip_z, close, wait for a grown-up to confirm the grip (Enter; no sensor, never judged automatically; grip_confirm_timeout_s then FAULT), up to travel_z, the fixed route_xy (no free search), the collection spot (collect_xy, down to collect_z, collect_dwell_s), the jig back to its stand, safe_z, park_xy. Every point inside the soft limits and every segment clear of keep_out [x0, y0, x1, y1] is checked before moving. Only magnetic test objects (paper clips): pencils and erasers are not collected. Keep magnets away from children's mouths and electronics. real: off (enabled_real false) and every null measured / confirmed item set on the machine before it may run (NOT measured yet). dry_run: the mock robot only; auto_confirm_grip_s (dry run only) confirms by itself after that many seconds.

auto_catch._note: One-button auto catch (backend/src/corexy_ufo_backend/sequence/). Z in the backend's z units (robot.z_min..z_max; z_max = arm at the top, the z_set top reference), XY in mm, times in s. 'real' drives the real crane: every null must be measured on the machine and every 'confirmed' item set true by hand after checking it there, otherwise the backend refuses auto_catch on the real robot. 'dry_run' is used only with --mock / --auto-catch-dry-run: made-up values for the virtual crane, never for the real robot. Accelerations and the servo speed are fixed in the firmware (XY 1000 mm/s^2, servo 2400 counts/s): they only drive the dry-run model. Polarity: the home limit switches are read by the firmware (active LOW, 30 ms debounce) and reach the host as LIMIT_X/LIMIT_Y=ACTIVE|OPEN; there is no physical E-stop input (stop = ABORT command); the catch button is the game's C key (no electrical polarity).
